what_it_does: Football modelling library with Poisson, Dixon-Coles, bivariate Poisson, negative binomial, Weibull-copula and Bayesian goal models plus implied-odds de-vigging and RPS scoring.
lesson_for_system: It offers several de-vig methods and many score models side by side, so the system should benchmark its single independent Poisson fit against Dixon-Coles and bivariate alternatives on the same data.

what_it_does: R package fitting Poisson, negative binomial, Dixon-Coles, CMP and hurdle goal models with time-weighting and an ML estimate of the Dixon-Coles rho.
lesson_for_system: Its explicit low-score dependence and 0-0 hurdle options show that an independent Poisson underprices draws and unders, which matters for the remaining-goals O/U lines the system trades.

what_it_does: R package for Dixon-Coles style team-strength soccer models with tidy interfaces.
lesson_for_system: It treats the model as a fitted, inspectable statistical object with standard errors, which the system lacks when it backs Poisson rates out of a single bookmaker's prices.

what_it_does: Stan-based R package for Bayesian static and dynamic bivariate Poisson, Skellam and Student-t football models with posterior predictive checks.
lesson_for_system: It produces full posterior uncertainty and model-comparison diagnostics, while the system outputs point probabilities with no uncertainty band to gate stakes.

what_it_does: Blog notebooks including a widely cited Python Dixon-Coles implementation and time-decay weighting walkthrough; tutorial quality, not a package.
lesson_for_system: It demonstrates the rho correction and xi time-decay explicitly, two components missing from a plain independent Poisson re-pricer.

what_it_does: Python implementations of Poisson goal prediction, Shin de-vigging, Elo and related soccer analytics methods; small and inactive.
lesson_for_system: It pairs Shin's method with the score model, a reminder that the input to the system's Poisson inversion should be de-vigged with a favourite-longshot-aware method, not proportional normalisation.

what_it_does: Single-notebook Dixon-Coles score predictor; toy.
lesson_for_system: Even toy Dixon-Coles repos include the low-score correction that the system's independent Poisson omits.

what_it_does: Small Dixon-Coles script used to win an office World Cup prediction contest; toy.
lesson_for_system: It optimises for the contest's scoring rule rather than raw accuracy, which mirrors the need for the system to optimise for betting return net of margin, not fit quality.

what_it_does: Student Bayesian Skellam goal-difference model after Karlis and Ntzoufras; toy.
lesson_for_system: Modelling goal difference directly via Skellam is a cheaper consistency check for the system's Asian handicap re-pricing than deriving it from two independent Poisson marginals.

what_it_does: Notebook implementing a Weibull count model for football scores; toy.
lesson_for_system: Weibull count models relax the equidispersion assumption, and the system has never tested whether remaining-goal counts are over- or under-dispersed relative to Poisson.

what_it_does: Calibrates live Poisson rates from market 1X2 and O/U prices and computes post-goal Skellam probabilities, validated against exchange orderbook data; toy-scale.
lesson_for_system: It is architecturally the same as the system and only claims to anticipate the market's post-goal repricing, which shows that inverting market prices yields market-consistent, not market-beating, probabilities.

what_it_does: Live win-probability project using non-homogeneous Poisson intensities, kernel-smoothed time-varying scoring rates and continuous-time Markov chains; academic toy.
lesson_for_system: It estimates a time-varying goal intensity curve, whereas a constant remaining-rate assumption misprices late-game and stoppage-time goal probability.

what_it_does: Dixon-Coles double-Poisson engine with live updating and per-league frozen verification ledgers that record predictions before results.
lesson_for_system: Its pre-registered, frozen prediction ledger is an evaluation discipline the system should copy so that model changes cannot be judged on hindsight.

what_it_does: Elo plus Dixon-Coles plus Monte Carlo tournament model, kept running year-round; hobby scale.
lesson_for_system: It combines a rating prior with the score model, while the system's in-play prices have no independent team-strength prior separate from the one bookmaker it trades against.

what_it_does: Open-source in-play probability, price and position-sizing tool for football trophy markets; toy.
lesson_for_system: Pairing in-play probability with explicit position sizing is useful, but its zero adoption and absence of a public track record make it a caution, not a reference.

what_it_does: Event-driven betting trading framework for Betfair with simulation, market recording, order lifecycle and middleware for in-play strategies.
lesson_for_system: It backtests on recorded tick-level market streams with realistic order matching, which is the standard the system's simulated ROI should meet before trusting it.

what_it_does: betfairlightweight, a Betfair API-NG wrapper with streaming market data.
lesson_for_system: Exchange prices with low margin provide a sharper reference than a single bookmaker's in-play line for checking whether the system's probabilities are really off-market.

what_it_does: Implements Shin's method for converting bookmaker odds to implied probabilities with insider-trading adjustment.
lesson_for_system: De-vigging the input lines with Shin rather than proportional normalisation changes the Poisson rates the system backs out, especially for longshot correct-score and handicap legs.

what_it_does: R package of de-vig methods including basic, Shin, power, additive, odds-ratio and others for converting odds to probabilities.
lesson_for_system: Having many de-vig methods side by side lets the system measure how sensitive its re-priced AH lines are to the margin-removal assumption.

what_it_does: Margin decomposition algorithms including multiplicative, additive, power and Shin; new and unadopted.
lesson_for_system: Its existence is mainly confirmation that margin removal is a model choice, which the system should record and test rather than hard-code.

what_it_does: Converts event-stream data to SPADL and values player actions with VAEP and expected threat.
lesson_for_system: Action-value models use in-match events, not prices, so they are a genuinely independent signal the system does not have.

what_it_does: Standardises tracking and event data from many providers into one model.
lesson_for_system: Provider-agnostic data loading is how mature projects avoid tying the model to one feed, while the system is tied to one bookmaker's feed for both input and target.

what_it_does: Streams StatsBomb event data, free and commercial, into Python.
lesson_for_system: Free StatsBomb event data allows building an xG-based live intensity model that is not derived from the same odds being bet into.

what_it_does: Free StatsBomb event data for selected competitions.
lesson_for_system: A public, versioned dataset makes model results reproducible, which the system's private PG data and shifting sample cannot offer.

what_it_does: Scrapers for Club Elo, ESPN, FBref, Football-Data.co.uk, Sofascore, SoFIFA, Understat and WhoScored with caching.
lesson_for_system: Football-Data.co.uk closing odds via this library give a free multi-bookmaker benchmark for testing whether the system's edge survives against closing lines.

what_it_does: R wrapper for FBref, Transfermarkt and Understat data; now archived.
lesson_for_system: Archival of a popular scraper shows data-source fragility, which argues for logging raw inputs in the system rather than relying on re-scraping.

what_it_does: Asynchronous Python client for Understat xG data.
lesson_for_system: Shot-level xG per match is an available pre-match strength input that would give the system a prior not contaminated by the trading bookmaker.

what_it_does: R client for Understat data; inactive.
lesson_for_system: Same lesson as the Python client, available xG features exist but are not used by the system.

what_it_does: Package for training and analysing expected goals models with calibration diagnostics.
lesson_for_system: It ships calibration curves alongside the xG model, a reporting habit the system's market-offset model should adopt.

what_it_does: Tutorial on cross-validating and calibrating expected-goals models, written by a betting-industry modeller.
lesson_for_system: It shows that probability calibration must be validated out of sample by time, matching the leakage fix the system only recently applied.

what_it_does: Python scrapers for FBref, Sofascore, Understat, Transfermarkt and other soccer sources.
lesson_for_system: Live Sofascore-style event feeds could supply red cards, shots and pressure indicators that the system's price-only model ignores.

what_it_does: Pipeline that extracts and publishes cleaned Transfermarkt datasets of games, lineups and valuations.
lesson_for_system: Squad value and lineup data are cheap structural strength features that are independent of in-play prices.

what_it_does: Python package for loading and analysing sports tracking and event data across providers.
lesson_for_system: It enforces unified data models and tests, illustrating the engineering hygiene expected before data feed a betting model.

what_it_does: Reads, synchronises and preprocesses soccer event and tracking data.
lesson_for_system: Explicit synchronisation of event and tracking timestamps is the analogue of the system's need to align price snapshots with match-clock events.

what_it_does: Football pitch plotting library for matplotlib.
lesson_for_system: Visual diagnostics are standard in mature projects, while the system lacks routine plots of predicted against realised goal rates by minute.

what_it_does: Curated collection of football analytics projects, data sources and tutorials.
lesson_for_system: It is a reference index, useful mainly for locating independent data the system could use as features.

what_it_does: Introductory soccer analytics handbook with notebooks.
lesson_for_system: Its baseline-first approach, starting from simple models and measuring improvement, is the discipline the system skipped when adding the LLM arm.

what_it_does: Teaching code from the Soccermatics course including xG and Poisson match simulation.
lesson_for_system: It simulates matches from shot-level rates, showing an alternative way to get remaining-goal distributions that does not depend on bookmaker lines.

what_it_does: R package for streaming StatsBomb data with API credentials.
lesson_for_system: Same data as statsbombpy, confirming event data is accessible in both main analytics languages.

what_it_does: Plots soccer event data in R ggplot2.
lesson_for_system: Not directly relevant to pricing, included for breadth of the data-tooling ecosystem.

what_it_does: Sports betting toolkit that wraps scikit-learn estimators as bettors and backtests value-bet strategies with time-series splits on historical odds.
lesson_for_system: Its built-in backtest uses time-ordered splits and market-maximum odds, the evaluation the system's logistic offset model should pass before live staking.

what_it_does: GUI app that trains neural nets and random forests on team-form features and Football-Data odds to suggest bets.
lesson_for_system: It reports accuracy-style metrics without a public betting record, a pattern to avoid because accuracy does not imply return after margin.

what_it_does: Statistical and ML model for top European leagues, evaluated by leave-one-season-out betting simulation with capped Kelly staking and a held-out final season.
lesson_for_system: Leave-one-season-out evaluation with a locked final test season is stricter than a single train-test split and suits the system's limited sample.

what_it_does: Neural-network time-series model for EPL double-chance bets; README reports a best-run ROI of 33.4% on 32 bets over 113 days.
lesson_for_system: A best-of-many ROI on 32 bets is selection-biased noise, so the system must report all configurations tried and require hundreds of out-of-sample bets.

what_it_does: Machine-learning classifiers predicting EPL match results; student project.
lesson_for_system: Classifier accuracy around chance-plus-a-bit is typical, showing why the system's metrics must be log loss or Brier versus the market, not hit rate.

what_it_does: ML system predicting over or under 2.5 goals from team statistics.
lesson_for_system: It targets the same O/U market as the system but from pre-match features, offering an independent comparison point.

what_it_does: ML pipeline forecasting soccer outcomes with feature engineering and model stacking.
lesson_for_system: Stacked models add complexity without a guaranteed edge, so the system should require each added arm to beat the market-only baseline.

what_it_does: Gradient-boosted tree library widely used in match predictors.
lesson_for_system: Gradient boosting is the common ML baseline that the system's small logistic offset should be compared against on identical time-split data.

what_it_does: Natural gradient boosting for probabilistic prediction with full predictive distributions, including Poisson.
lesson_for_system: NGBoost can predict a Poisson goal-rate distribution from features directly, an alternative to backing rates out of one bookmaker's prices.

what_it_does: Ensemble EPL predictor with 13 base learners and Dixon-Coles; hobby project.
lesson_for_system: Large ensembles without pre-registered evaluation are easy to overfit, which argues for the system keeping its model small and its test strict.

what_it_does: Proper scoring rules including CRPS and Brier score; archived but stable.
lesson_for_system: Proper scoring rules let the system compare its probabilities with the de-vigged market on the same matches, which hit rate and ROI alone cannot do.

what_it_does: Actively maintained library for probabilistic forecast evaluation with CRPS, log score and energy scores.
lesson_for_system: CRPS on the full remaining-goals distribution evaluates every O/U line at once, a better test of the Poisson model than per-bet outcomes.

what_it_does: net:cal library for measuring and correcting miscalibration with ECE, reliability diagrams, histogram binning, isotonic and beta calibration.
lesson_for_system: Reliability diagrams by probability bucket would show whether the system's edge sits in regions where it is miscalibrated.

what_it_does: Toolbox for predictive uncertainty quantification, calibration metrics and recalibration.
lesson_for_system: It treats uncertainty as a measured output, while the system bets fixed stakes regardless of how uncertain the model is.

what_it_does: Reference implementation of temperature scaling for neural network calibration.
lesson_for_system: A one-parameter recalibration on a held-out time slice is a cheap fix to test before adding new model arms.

what_it_does: Beta calibration for binary classifiers.
lesson_for_system: Beta calibration handles probabilities near 0 and 1 better than Platt scaling, relevant for late-match O/U legs with extreme prices.

what_it_does: Venn-ABERS calibration producing probability intervals for binary and multi-class predictions.
lesson_for_system: Venn-ABERS intervals give a probability range per bet, and stakes should be skipped when the range contains the market price.

what_it_does: Conformal prediction intervals and risk control for scikit-learn models.
lesson_for_system: Conformal risk control offers a distribution-free way to cap the error rate of the system's bet-selection filter.

what_it_does: TrueSkill Bayesian rating system implementation.
lesson_for_system: Bayesian ratings carry an explicit uncertainty term, an idea the system could use for team strength priors.

what_it_does: Glicko-2 rating implementation with rating deviation and volatility.
lesson_for_system: Rating deviation shrinks bets on teams with little recent data, which the system does not account for.

what_it_does: OpenSkill multiplayer Bayesian rating system, a faster open alternative to TrueSkill.
lesson_for_system: Fast online rating updates could supply a per-team prior that is refreshed every match without depending on bookmaker prices.

what_it_does: Compares Elo, Glicko, TrueSkill, Bradley-Terry and other rating algorithms behind one interface with benchmarking.
lesson_for_system: Comparing rating systems under one harness is the same head-to-head evaluation the system should run across its Poisson, logistic and LLM arms.

what_it_does: Simple Elo rating library; toy.
lesson_for_system: Elo is the minimum independent strength baseline, and the system has none.

what_it_does: Dynamic, contamination-free benchmark of LLM forecasting accuracy with superforecaster and public comparison groups.
lesson_for_system: Its published leaderboard has shown the best LLMs still trailing superforecasters, so the system's LLM arm should be assumed to have no edge until it beats the market on Brier.

what_it_does: Framework for building AI forecasting bots for Metaculus tournaments with research and aggregation utilities.
lesson_for_system: Bots built on it are scored against community and pro forecasters, a benchmark structure the system's LLM arm lacks.

what_it_does: Simple template bot for forecasting in Metaculus AI benchmark tournaments.
lesson_for_system: Its quarterly tournaments report bots below the pro-forecaster baseline, consistent with treating LLM sports picks as unproven.

what_it_does: Autocast dataset and code from NeurIPS 2022 on forecasting world events with retrieval-augmented language models.
lesson_for_system: The paper's models stayed well below human crowd accuracy, another sign that LLM forecasts are a weak signal against an efficient market.

what_it_does: Pre-registered, continuously scored football forecasts from 43 LLMs across five European leagues plus a frozen World Cup archive.
lesson_for_system: Pre-registration with git-tagged predictions is the evaluation the system's LLM arm needs before any staking.

what_it_does: Frozen pre-tournament World Cup predictions from about ten frontier LLMs scored by accuracy, Brier score and ROI against Polymarket.
lesson_for_system: Scoring LLM picks against a prediction-market price is exactly the comparison that determines whether an LLM arm adds value.

what_it_does: MIRAI benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on international event forecasting with temporal cutoffs.
lesson_for_system: Strict temporal cutoffs on retrieved context are needed so an LLM arm cannot leak post-kickoff information into backtests.
